capabilities: Draw a rooted family tree of the active note's parent/child links
Switch between drawn tree, phylogenetic tree and collapsible outline
Show breadcrumbs at the top of notes that have a parent
Render subtrees inside notes with a branching-toc code block
Create child or parent notes and generate a table-of-contents note
disambiguation: Not a folder- or heading-based table-of-contents generator; the hierarchy comes only from parent and child properties in note frontmatter.
extras: Free and open source, MIT licensed, no network requests, works on mobile. Part of the author's Companion suite of local-first plugins, but the only one with no AI model. Beta versions are published as GitHub pre-releases for BRAT. README includes benchmark tables for vaults up to 20,000 notes and a sample-vault/ folder; demo GIF listed as coming soon.
intentEvidence: drawn as a real branching tree instead of the tangled graph view
problem: Obsidian's graph view shows every link around a note without direction, so a parent/child hierarchy cannot be read as a hierarchy.

relations.evidence: install BRAT, choose Add beta plugin, paste TonyPeonio/obsidian-branching-table-of-contents

summary: Sidebar and inline view that draws parent/child note properties as a rooted family tree of the current note, with breadcrumbs and outline modes.
